newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NFI 9 shows PLN 2.1 mln loss after audit.
newsitem.headline: Polish NFI 9 shows PLN 2.1 mln loss after audit.

text.p: Polish National Kwiatkowski Investment Fund (NFI no. 9) had a net loss of 2.14 million zlotys in 1996 according to its audited report, the fund's president said on Tuesday.
Earlier the fund said it had a net profit of 4.2 million zlotys last year.
"In 1996 the net loss was 2.14 million zlotys, but this year we have profits," Miroslaw Bojanczyk told a news conference. @
He explained the fund's auditor had demanded additional provisions be created by some companies in the fund's portfolio, which pushed down its 1996 results.
Bojanczyk also said Kwiatkowski wanted to sell some of the strategic 33-percent stakes in its portfolio, reducing them to between 16 and 20 from current 32.
"It (the reduction) will happen in the next few months...at the same time small minority stakes are being systematically sold," he said.
He said chemical, farm and construction sectors would be preferred in building the fund's portfolio.
Under the government's NFI programme, shares in about 500 mid-sized companies are allocated to 15 NFIs run by foreign and domestic management firms.
From May 12 the 26 million Poles who bought a participation unit in the scheme have been able to exchange it for 15 shares, one in each fund, which on Thursday will start trade on the Warsaw bourse.
The units lose their validity on December 31, 1998.
